question: What will be the 2-party Gallagher disproportionality index for North Carolina's House races in 2026?

calls.reasoning: The redrawn map targets 11R-3D, but 2026 looks like a Democratic wave: NC generic-ballot polls show D+6 to D+10 and Cooper leads Whatley by about 10. Markets make Davis (NC-1) about 80% and Ager (NC-11, Lean D) about 85%. Hudson (NC-9) is about 81% to hold. Expected R seats are about 9 of 14 (64.3%). I put the GOP two-party House vote near 48-49%, allowing for 2024's roughly 3.7pt House-over-presidential R skew. That gives about 16 at R 9 seats and about 22 at R 10, so the outcome is bimodal and seat count dominates. Above 30 would need an 11-3 sweep on a sub-48.6% R vote; below 5 would need R at 7 or fewer seats. No market on the index itself was found; the only markets are per-district winner markets on Polymarket/Kalshi.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off 2026 NC US House results: |GOP share of 14 seats − GOP share of R+D two-party House vote|. Each seat = 7.14 pts. Event window: general election 2026-11-03 → certified results; as of 2026-10-29 the election has not occurred.
- Map: the 2025 mid-decade redraw shifted NC-1 rightward, targeting 11R-3D (Brennan Center background).
- 2024 baseline (Wikipedia): R 10 seats/4 D; R 2,889,657 votes (52.78%), D 2,328,248 (42.80%), so R two-party about 55.4% and Gallagher about 16.0. Trump two-party in NC 2024 was about 51.7, so the House vote ran about 3.7pt more R.
- NC-1 (Davis D-inc vs Buckhout R): Cook toss-up; GQR internal (D) Oct 8 shows Davis 50-45 allocated; poll average Davis 48-42; prediction markets about 80% Davis on ~$27k volume (NC Newsline 2026-10-29).
- NC-11 (open; Edwards not running amid allegations; Ager D): Cook moved to Lean D in Oct; markets have Ager above 85%; Edwards won by 13 in 2024.
- NC-9 (Hudson R-inc vs Ojeda D): Cook Safe R (Oct 16); poll average Hudson +4 (46-42); Polymarket Hudson about 81%.
- Statewide environment: Senate Cooper leads Whatley by 10-14 (Carolina Journal 49.4-39.1; Elon 52-39; HPU 54-40; RCP average +10.6). Generic House ballot: HPU/YouGov D 52-43; Carolina Journal D 49.1-43.2 (narrowed from D+9.2 in Sept); AARP D+10.
- Seat scenarios map to roughly: R11 → about 28-29; R10 → about 21-23; R9 → about 15-17; R8 → about 9-11; R7 → about 2-4 (depending on R two-party vote of about 47-50%).
- Searched but not found: a market on the statewide vote share or the index itself; ratings for NC-13/NC-6/NC-14/NC-3 (presumed R-favored); whether every district is contested by both parties (an uncontested seat would skew the vote totals).
calls.reference_class: Seat-vote Gallagher gaps for NC House delegations under GOP-drawn maps (2024: 71.4% seats vs 55.4% two-party vote = 16.0)

calls.reasoning: The 2025 map was drawn 11R-3D. NC-1 (Davis D, Toss Up; Kalshi ~83% Davis) and NC-11 (Edwards R withdrew after an ethics scandal; Cook Lean D) are the swing seats, with NC-3/5/9 long shots. In 2024 Republicans got ~55.4% of the two-party House vote and won 10/14 seats, index ~16. A Democratic-leaning midterm puts the R two-party share near 49-53%. 9R gives an index of ~14, 10R ~20, 11R ~26, and the seat-vote correlation partly offsets. Market check: only a Kalshi NC-1 seat-winner market was found (not matched to this index); none on Polymarket/Manifold.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off the 2026 NC US House results: |GOP seat share - GOP share of the two-party (R+D) House vote| across all 14 districts. Event window: Nov 3, 2026 election -> certified results by ~Dec 1, 2026; as of Oct 29 the election hasn't happened (0% of results in).
- Seat-share steps: 11R=78.6%, 10R=71.4%, 9R=64.3%, 8R=57.1%, 7R=50%.
- The 2025 mid-decade redistricting redrew NC-1 to be more Republican; the map targets 11R-3D (Brennan Center background).
- 2024 baseline (Wikipedia): R 2,889,657 (52.78%), D 2,328,248 (42.80%), so R two-party share ~55.4%; seats 10R-4D; index ~16. That year the House vote ran ~2 pts more R than the presidential race (Trump ~51.6% two-party in NC).
- NC-1 (Davis D-inc vs Buckhout R): Cook moved it Lean R -> Toss Up. Polls: GQR (D) Davis +8; another Davis 50-43; co/efficient (R, Oct 8) Buckhout 43-42; NRCC internal (May) tied 41-41; average about Davis 46.3, Buckhout 41.8 (WITN Sep 15, poll aggregators). Davis has out-raised Buckhout by ~$1M.
- NC-11: Rep. Chuck Edwards (R) withdrew Aug 5, 2026 after an Ethics Committee censure recommendation over sexual misconduct (Ballotpedia, NC Newsline). Replacement Jennifer Balkcom (R) has struggled with fundraising; Jamie Ager (D) has raised millions. Cook rates it Lean D (Oct 23). Edwards won it by 13 in 2024.
- NC-3 (Hudson R, NRCC chair) vs Ojeda (D): Cook Solid R, PVI R+10; a HMP (D) internal has Ojeda within 4 with 12% undecided (WRAL, Oct 2026).
- NC-5 (Murphy R) and NC-9 (Knott R): Cook shifted them toward less certainty for Republicans (WRAL).
- WRAL reports that early voting shows Democratic and independent mobilization and lower Republican turnout; 70% of independents disapprove of Trump.
- Mechanism: Democratic seat gains come with a lower R vote share, which partly offsets the index change. Packed Democratic urban seats (NC-2, 4, 12) inflate the D vote.
- Market: a Kalshi NC-1 seat-winner market exists; no market on the index itself.
- Searched but not found: confirmation that all 14 districts are contested by both parties in 2026; the 2022 NC two-party House share.
calls.reference_class: NC US House elections under GOP-drawn maps (2024: 10/14 seats on ~55% two-party R vote, index ~16); midterm swing against the president's party

calls.reasoning: Index = |GOP seat% - GOP two-party vote%|. 2025 map built for 11R-3D; 2024 was 10R with 55.4% R two-party vote (index ~16). 2026 environment is strongly Democratic (NC HPU/YouGov generic ballot D 52-43; Sabato/Cook moved NC-1 and NC-11 toward D; NC-13 toss-up; NC-8/3/5 under pressure). Kalshi has Davis (NC-1) at roughly 65-83%. Seat-count probabilities ~ 12R 2%, 11R 18%, 10R 37%, 9R 31%, 8R or fewer 12%, with R vote ~47-50% -> outcomes clustered near 29, 22, 16, 11. No market on the index itself; Kalshi district markets used only as seat evidence.
calls.dossier:
- Resolution: |GOP % of 14 NC House seats - GOP % of two-party (R+D) House vote summed across all districts|; resolves off 2026 certified/Wikipedia results, not polls. Event window: Nov 3 2026 election -> results by 2026-12-01; as of 2026-10-29 voting not yet complete (early voting under way).
- Seat-share steps: 11R=78.57%, 10R=71.43%, 9R=64.29%, 8R=57.14%, 12R=85.71%.
- 2024 (Wikipedia): R 2,889,657 vs D 2,328,248 -> R two-party 55.4%; 10R-4D; index ~16. Trump won NC by ~3 in 2024.
- 2018 D-wave year (background knowledge): NC R two-party House share ~51%, 10R-3D (13 seats), index ~26.
- 2025 mid-decade redistricting redrew NC-1 to target Rep. Don Davis (D); intended 11R-3D map.
- NC-1: Cook moved Lean R -> Toss Up (Oct 2026); Sabato Lean D (Oct 20). Polls last 30 days avg Davis 46.3 / Buckhout 41.8 (RedBox (D) Oct 20-23: 45-44; co/efficient (R) Oct 6-8: 42-43). Kalshi district market exists (Davis favored; quoted values range in snippets).
- NC-11: open seat (Edwards withdrew); D Jamie Ager vs R Jennifer Balkcom; Sabato Lean D (Oct 20), Cook Lean D per WRAL; Inside Elections Toss-up (Oct 15); Trump ~+9.5-11.5 in 2024.
- NC-13 rated Toss-up by one outlet (R+2 lean); NRCC disputes competitiveness.
- NC-8 (Hudson vs Ojeda): Cook Solid R, D internal poll Hudson +4 with 12% undecided; NRCC spending. NC-3, NC-5 rated with reduced R certainty.
- NC statewide polls Oct 2026: HPU/YouGov US House generic D 52 / R 43 (likely voters); Carolina Journal state legislature generic D-leaning.
- WRAL: early voting shows D and independent turnout up, R turnout down.
- Searched but not found: list of uncontested 2026 NC districts (none identified); any market on the statewide index or NC statewide House vote.
calls.reference_class: NC US House Gallagher-style 2-party index under GOP-drawn maps, 2016-2024 (2016 ~23, 2018 ~26, 2024 ~16)

calls.reasoning: The 2025 map was drawn for 11R-3D, but a Democratic-leaning midterm (NC generic ballot D+6-9, Cooper +10) and the district markets (NC-1 Davis ~65-83%, NC-11 Ager ~85%) make 9R the modal outcome, with a GOP two-party House vote of about 48.5%, which gives an index of about 16. The 10R scenario (~27%, vote about 50%) gives about 21.5. The 8R tail (~13%) gives about 10, and an 11R sweep (~4%) gives about 27-28. 2024 baseline: 10R on 55.4% two-party, index about 16.
calls.reconciliation: Factual disputes: district labels for Hudson (NC-3/8/9) and NC-5/9/13 could not be settled without web access, but they don't change the seat-count logic. Whether all districts are contested is unconfirmed; that uncertainty is folded into the vote-share spread. On judgment, I side with Runs 1-2 (9R modal) over Run 3's heavier 10R/11R weighting, because the district markets and the D+6-9 generic ballot both point to a Democratic sweep of NC-1 and NC-11 as most likely. Run 2's vote-share range (49-53%) looks too Republican for a 9R world with the generic ballot at D+6-9; I use about 48.5%, consistent with Run 1. Run 1's dispersion basis is broadly kept but tightened slightly.
